Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoForge Cloud Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoForge Cloud's results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on the call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Liam Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Product Officer; and Jordan Lee, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoForge Cloud delivered another strong Q3, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

Delving deeper into our cloud services revenue performance, which continues to power our business forward, we reported $25.6 billion in the quarter, reflecting an impressive 18% increase quarter-over-quarter from $21.7 billion in Q1 FY2024 and a robust 32% rise year-over-year from $19.4 billion in Q2 FY2023. This momentum highlights the strong demand for digital transformation, AI adoption, and cloud elasticity amid cost pressures on enterprises.

Breaking it down by segments, our Infrastructure-as-a-Service, or IaaS, which makes up 60% of cloud revenue at $15.4 billion, surged 22% quarter-over-quarter and 38% year-over-year. The surge was propelled by demand for hyperscale compute, especially our GPU-accelerated StratoForge Nitro instances featuring NVIDIA H100s and next-gen A100 equivalents. AI and machine learning workloads led the charge, with inference services growing 45% year-over-year as clients like a top financial services firm scaled real-time fraud detection and an autonomous vehicle leader ramped simulation training. Compute utilization reached 85% globally, up from 72% last year, thanks to our auto-scaling tools using predictive forecasting.

Platform-as-a-Service, or PaaS, added $6.4 billion, 25% of the mix, with 15% quarter-over-quarter and 28% year-over-year gains. Databases and analytics shone, as our managed Aurora-compatible service expanded 35% year-over-year from Oracle and SQL Server migrations. Our Kafka-compatible streaming service handled over 10 zettabytes of data, up 50% year-over-year, aiding e-commerce supply chain optimizations.

SaaS offerings, including collaboration and security, brought in $3.8 billion, up 12% quarter-over-quarter and 22% year-over-year. Zero-trust integrations with our cloud-native SIEM tools gained traction amid rising ransomware, securing multi-year deals worth $1.2 billion in annual contract value from enterprises aligning with NIST 800-53.

The quarter-over-quarter 18% lift came from seasonal factors and execution, including Q1 capacity adds of 2.5 million vCPUs in US East and EU West, ramping queued deployments. AI compute drove over 60% of incremental growth, with non-AI at 12%, plus 5% higher pricing on reserved instances amid GPU constraints.

Year-over-year, our 32% growth exceeded the industry's 25% per Synergy Research, gaining share against AWS and Azure through $12 billion in prior CapEx for data centers and five new sovereign regions. Our 300+ edge points of presence cut latency 25%, boosting low-latency inference.

Regionally, Americas at 50% or $12.8 billion grew 35% year-over-year, anchored by a $2.5 billion five-year AI training deal from a Big Tech leader in Northern Virginia and Oregon. EMEA, 25% or $6.4 billion, rose 30%, strong in Germany and UK sovereign zones for financials and autos. APAC, also 25% at $6.4 billion, advanced 28% despite forex, with Mumbai and Tokyo at 95% utilization for telco edge and GenAI with SoftBank-like partners.

We're prioritizing AI leadership via our Vertex AI-like foundation models service, attracting 5,000 developers in beta for $3 billion run-rate by FY2025; hybrid/multi-cloud orchestration winning VMware migrations; and sustainability with carbon-neutral centers and Spot efficiencies cutting TCO 30%. With RPO up 42% to $180 billion, we expect 28-30% year-over-year growth in Q4. Now I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased with our financial results for Q3. Revenue increased by 32% year-over-year to $25.6 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 72.4%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 32%.

Turning to our cost optimization initiatives, which have delivered substantial bottom-line benefits and set us up for sustained growth in this competitive hyperscaler environment fueled by AI/ML demand. In Q3, cost of revenues dropped 12% year-over-year to $4.2 billion despite the 32% revenue jump, expanding non-GAAP gross margins by 320 basis points to 72.4%—our best in three years. Quarter-over-quarter, COGS per revenue dollar improved 8% via efforts in infrastructure, software, procurement, and customer tools, leveraging our FinOps platform covering 95% of workloads across 45 regions and 150+ zones.

On infrastructure, we've shifted over 65% of instances to custom silicon like StratoForge Graviton4 ARM processors and Tensor cores for inference, offering 40% better price-performance than x86, saving $450 million in Q3—enough for 2.5 million LLM fine-tunings. Spot instance use rose to 42% for batch jobs on StratoForge S3 storage, with ML-driven Capacity Optimizer preempting 85% interruptions. Data center PPE grew only 5% YoY to $28 billion while handling 35% more petabytes via densification and liquid cooling.

Software-wise, FinOps adoption hit 78% with StratoForge Cost Explorer automating rightsizing and tagging, cutting idle capacity 22% in EKS Kubernetes environments. Serverless via StratoForge Lambda grew 55% quarter-over-quarter at 70% lower cost; Hybrid Optimizer for multi-cloud saved 15-20% on egress for 45% of enterprises.

Regionally, APAC optimizations in Singapore/Tokyo cut network opex 18%; EMEA's Dublin/Frankfurt hit PUE 1.08 on renewables, saving €220 million; Americas leveraged AI tailwinds. Procurement hedged DRAM/NAND for 16% COGS cuts, divesting legacy assets for $800 million redirected to R&D.

These efforts saved $1.2 billion in Q3, funding 25% R&D growth to $1.8 billion for post-quantum crypto and agentic AI. Savings Plans penetration at 62% locked $12 billion commitments. Targeting 75% gross margins by FY25 with quantum optimization and edge expansions. Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Liam Chen, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation StratoForge Serverless platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

A critical part of this has been our investments in security infrastructure and personnel, positioning us as a leader where threats have risen 62% year-over-year per Verizon DBIR, with ransomware up 150% and AI attacks at 28% per CrowdStrike. In Q3, we committed $285 million, up 38% year-over-year, or 14.2% of $2.01 billion R&D—on pace for $1.15 billion full-year, 42% growth or 11.8% of revenue. Infrastructure CapEx was $162 million for firewalls, enclaves, confidential computing; personnel $123 million, growing team 28% to 4,200 FTEs at $285,000 average comp.

Driven by 45% more customer audits from NIS2 and SEC rules, our zero-trust with Istio meshes cut lateral risks 92%. ML threat detection via Graph Neural Networks in StratoForge Sentinel caught 17,000 anomalies, 98% APTs early. $40 million in post-quantum Kyber/Dilithium for enclaves. Hired 320 experts, Security Academy certified 1,200.

Regionally: EMEA 32% budget for GDPR sovereigns; APAC 28% for DPDP/IRAP; U.S. federal 22% for IL5, winning $2.4 billion DoD. ROI: 97.8% retention, NPS 68, $450 million breaches avoided. Guiding 35-40% growth in 2025 for blockchain and GenAI red-teaming. Now, I'll pass it over to Sophia Grant for a product roadmap update.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are excited about the market reception to our new StratoForge AI Suite offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the enterprise AI and machine learning sector.

Integral to this roadmap are our achievements in security and compliance certifications, a key differentiator in this competitive market. In Q3, we secured 12 new certifications, totaling 178 globally—up 22% year-over-year, outpacing peers in regulated sectors.

In the U.S., FedRAMP High for Sovereign Cloud after 18-month, 400-control audit covers 95% workloads, boosting federal bookings 35% quarter-over-quarter, including a $250 million defense deal—one of six providers. EU: GDPR Article 28 with ISO 27701 across 27 states/UK, zero major findings by Deloitte; ISO 27017/18 drove 28% financial adoption, like 40 PB bank migration. APAC: Australia's IRAP PROTECTED, Singapore MTCS Level 3 for $1.2 billion government market.

Healthcare/fintech: PCI DSS 4.0 Level 1 with <1% vulnerabilities under 2 Tbps DDoS; HITRUST CSF r2 for ePHI, now 15% Q3 ARR. These drove 42% bookings from BFSI/gov/healthcare, 28% segment growth. Our Compliance Engine uses AI for 99.99% audit readiness, cutting TCO 18%.

Backed by $450 million FY24 CapEx: zero-trust Envoy, PQC Kyber in S3, 300% Bug Bounty (1,200 vulns), SGX/SEV-SNP enclaves. Ahead: ISO 42001 AI, SOC 3, CMMC 2.0 amid $50B compliance spend by 2026, 62% threat surge. Compliance powers 68% multi-cloud barriers overcome. I'll now hand it over to Jordan Lee to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Sophia. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

As part of building market momentum, we've aligned our go-to-market strategies with forward-looking revenue guidance for the cloud segment and full company. Following Q3's $3.52 billion total revenue—beating midpoint by 2%, with cloud at $2.48 billion up 28% year-over-year, AI/ML 42% surge—we're optimistic based on $45 billion RPO up 35%.

For Q4, cloud segment $2.82 billion to $2.88 billion, 25-28% year-over-year: PaaS 35%, IaaS 22%; AI/HPC 45% growth like H100 clusters; top-20 customers 32%, NRR 118%; Americas 55% up 30%, EMEA 25% up 40%, APAC 20% up 25%. Full company $3.95 billion to $4.02 billion, 22-24%; EPS $1.42-$1.48, margins 31-33%, $150 million AI CapEx.

Raised FY24: cloud $10.54-$10.74 billion, 27-29%; full $14.62-$14.88 billion, 24-26%, op income $4.65-$4.75 billion, EPS $5.68-$5.82. Visibility from 85% RPO conversion; ForgeEdge $500 million contracts; zero-trust SASE 50% growth; PUE 1.15. Risks: macro SMB, APAC geo; gaining AI share at 28% win rates. Doubling 'StratoForge Everywhere' for hybrid, Snowflake/Databricks integrations Q1 FY25; targeting 30%+ FY25 growth.

Back to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Finally, on our capital expenditure outlook and plans, we're guiding FY2024 to $28-$30 billion, 22% of revenue run-rate, up 15% year-over-year—$18.5 billion through Q3, Q4 $7.5-$8 billion. Data centers 65%/$19 billion, network 20%/$6 billion, servers 15%/$4.5 billion; stable at 20-22% of revenue.

FY2025 $32-$35 billion, 12-15% up for AI, geo expansion, efficiency; peaking mid-decade at 85-90% utilization. Supply chain locked 70% silicon.

Pillars: 15 new regions/45 AZs, 2.5M sq ft, Nexus campuses 500MW liquid-cooled PUE<1.15, 60% renewables. AI: $8 billion for 50k+ H100/H200, Ion TPUs, 100PB NVMe. Networking/edge: $6.5 billion 400Gbps, 200 Outposts.

Regions: NA 50%/$16B AI hubs; EMEA 25%/$8B sovereigns; APAC 18%/$6B Chennai 300MW; LatAm/MEA 7%. First-mover in AI everywhere, hybrid Fabric SDN; microgrids for 2030 carbon-neutral. Efficiency: 70% utilization in 12 months, 3-4x revenue multiples, 25-30% FCF. With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Sarah Kline with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, can you elaborate on the sustainability of AI-driven growth given GPU constraints and potential capex intensity? How do you see margins holding?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. AI growth remains a core tailwind, with our custom TPUs and partnerships ensuring supply beyond peers. We've structured multi-year commitments converting RPO efficiently, and as utilization hits 85%, margins will expand to mid-30s. Our FinOps and spot utilization keep us ahead on efficiency.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Great, thanks. Marcus, on capex outlook, how are you balancing AI investments with free cash flow generation, especially with FY25 guidance?

Marcus Hale:
Appreciate it, David. Our $32-35 billion FY25 CapEx is targeted, with 70% utilization ramps delivering 3-4x returns. FCF stays at 25-30% of revenue through disciplined allocation—65% data centers, renewables-integrated—and divestitures. We're funding repurchases while scaling AI sustainably.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
